title: The Trail Camera
hook: My neighbor had one rule about my new trail camera: if it ever takes a picture of you, don't go out to check it.
lines: Something kept digging up my garden at night. So I strapped a trail camera to the old oak in my yard.
My neighbor, old Mr. Dale, watched from his porch... and gave me one rule.
If that camera ever takes a picture of you... don't go out to check it.
For two weeks, it sent photos to my phone every night. Deer. Raccoons. A fox.
Then, at three-twelve a.m., my phone buzzed.
It was me. Barefoot. In my pajamas. Standing in the wet grass... staring into the lens.
I don't sleepwalk. And every door was still locked... from the inside.
The next night, another photo. Me again. Closer. Smiling.
So tonight, I sat on my bed in the dark, holding my phone.
The photo was of my bedroom window. Taken from the oak tree.
And sitting on my bed, behind the glass, holding a phone... was me.
I looked up. Out in the yard, the camera's red light was blinking.
And beside it, in my pajamas, wearing my face... something waved me outside.
